sentences.text: The defining bone of this animal is a right ilium, a hip bone, with a partial femur possibly serving as a paratype.
This ilium features a thickened ridge above the supra-acetabular crest, a trait found in many paracrocodylomorphs.
The femur lacks an intertrochanteric fossa and has a low fourth trochanter, features consistent with proterosuchids, Euparkeria, and archosaurs.
A groove on the proximal surface of the femur is a character shared with paracrocodylomorphs and some dinosauriforms.
The genus Vytshegdus was named by Andreii Sennikov in 1988.
The genus contains only one known species, Vytshegdosuchus zheshartensis.
Fossils of Vytshegdosuchus come from the Early Triassic (latest Olenekian stage) of the Komi Republic in Russia.
Specimens were found in the Zheshart locality along the Vychegda River within the Parotosuchus fauna of the Upper Yarenskian Gorizont.
The holotype represents the oldest known archosaur material from Russia and the only one from the Early Triassic period.
A 2011 numerical phylogenetic analysis by Nesbitt placed Vytshegdosuchus within the Paracrocodylomorpha.
Vytshegdosuchus was originally classified in the Rauisuchidae family based on similarities to other loricatan archosaurs.
Nesbitt (2009) suggested that Vytshegdosuchus is an archosaur belonging to the Paracrocodylomorpha.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Vytshegdosuchus as Paracrocodylomorpha.
It is debated whether isolated bones from widely separated localities can be confidently assigned to Vytshegdosuchus.
